business_problem: Business decision makers had to review multiple websites, including information irrelevant to their circumstances, to find funding support. The department wanted to surface relevant opportunities and summaries based on a user's location, business sector, business age, and revenue.
solution_summary: DBT's BGS pipeline gathers funding-opportunity text from Innovate UK and GOV.UK (including the GOV.UK Content API) using scheduled Elastic Container Service tasks coordinated by Amazon Eventbridge. Scraped text is cleaned by the Presidio PII scrubber, enriched with opportunity and date metadata, split into 300-word chunks with 20-word overlap, embedded by Amazon Titan Text Embeddings v2, and stored in an OpenSearch vector database. On a user request from business.gov.uk, API Gateway and Simple Queue Service (SQS) route session inputs to Lambda functions, which map predefined answers, retrieve relevant documents, and call Amazon Bedrock. Anthropic Claude 3.7 Sonnet generates personalized funding summaries; output is HTML-formatted and returned with source links. A temporary cache supports repeat requests, while samples and feedback go to DBT's internal workspace for monthly evaluation.

data_flow: Scheduled ECS tasks gather Innovate UK and GOV.UK opportunity pages, including through the GOV.UK Content API; Catapult UK is also named as a backend data source. Presidio removes PII, then content is chunked, embedded with Titan Text Embeddings v2, and stored in OpenSearch. business.gov.uk sends predefined session inputs through API Gateway and SQS to Lambda; the backend retrieves relevant documents and sends context and a prompt to Bedrock/Claude 3.7 Sonnet. HTML-formatted summaries and source links return to the user; samples and feedback are transferred to DBT's internal workspace.

evidence_quotes: Users previously would need to review multiple websites to check if any support was available for their Business, likely requiring the user to read content that was not relevant to them.
These embeddings are used in a vector search to find the most relevant documents to a user input.
The information received from the client is converted into a prompt and sent to Bedrock.
This tool provides a time saving for the user seeking information and provides greater visibility of available relevant funding support to users.
The model was able to perform well with no links being hallucinated/modified from the original source link.
